sources.title: What’s in a Name? Uncovering Early Women Computers
sources.locator: Paragraph identifying Nancy McCandlish Prichard's three years at the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory before OSS service
sources.rights_notes: The article states that the chronology was confirmed in Smithsonian Annual Reports and the Washington Post obituary. The source spells the role 'Special Assistant to the Meterologist'; the project normalizes only the obvious typographical error in the role field.

sources.title: Nancy Prichard; Church and Civic Volunteer
sources.rights_notes: Used as corroboration for the full name, Smithsonian employment, civilian OSS status, and Cairo service. The later family and medical details are not stored or published.

organizations.normalization_notes: The Observatory is preserved as the historical employing unit rather than silently collapsed into its parent, the Smithsonian Institution.

affiliations.date_precision: The Smithsonian source documents three years immediately before she joined OSS during World War II; exact start and end dates are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: The Smithsonian source calls her Special Assistant to the Meteorologist at SAO; the Washington Post describes her as administrative assistant to the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution. Both source wordings are retained in the claim evidence.

claims.claim_text: Nancy McCandlish Prichard worked at the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory for three years immediately before joining OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: worked as a Special Assistant to the Meterologist at SAO for three years before joining the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Smithsonian Archives explicitly places her three-year Observatory role before OSS; the Washington Post independently describes Smithsonian administrative employment followed by civilian OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity supported by the distinctive full name, employer, OSS status, Cairo assignment, and indexed adjacency to Edgar Prichard.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate pre-OSS employment and last documented civilian employer before wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The two sources use different role wording but agree on the Smithsonian employer and sequence. The Observatory is preserved as the historical employing unit.
